nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-01.title: Combine the terms
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-01.body:
$N+0.802N+0.7605N=2.5625N=\frac{41}{16}N$. For this to be a prime, $\frac{41N}{16}$ must be an integer, so $16\mid N$; writing $N=16m$ gives $41m$, which is prime only when $m=1$. So $N=16$ (giving $41$).

**Answer: 16**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-02.title: Pythagorean theorem
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-02.body:
$AB^2+BC^2=(BC+2)^2$ gives $AB^2=4BC+4$, so $AB$ is even and $BC=\frac{AB^2}{4}-1$. The perimeter grows with $AB$, so take the least even $AB>50$: $AB=52$, $BC=\frac{2704}{4}-1=675$ (and $AC=677$).

**Answer: 675**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-03.title: Area two ways
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-03.body:
Adjacent sides satisfy $MA+MH=30$. The area is $4\cdot MA=8\cdot MH$, so $MA=2\,MH$. Then $3\,MH=30$, $MH=10$, and the longer side is $MA=20$.

**Answer: 20**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-04.title: Step by step
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-04.body:
First tile T: $\frac15$. Then E: $\frac34$. Then P: $\frac13$. The last two are E's for sure. Probability: $\frac15\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac13=\frac1{20}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{20}$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-04.title: Count arrangements
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-04.body:
The letters E, E, E, T, P have $\frac{5!}{3!}=20$ equally likely distinct arrangements, and TEPEE is one of them: $\frac1{20}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{20}$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-06.title: Symmetric slopes
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-06.body:
The two lines meet where $2x+2=0.5x-4$, i.e. at $(-4,-6)$; the mirror passes through this point. Reflection in a line of slope $1$ swaps $x$ and $y$ directions, taking slope $\frac12$ to slope $2$. So the mirror is the line of slope $1$ through $(-4,-6)$: $y=x-2$, which has positive integers $a=1$, $b=2$. (The other bisector has slope $-1$, which would give $a<0$.)

**Answer: $(1, 2)$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-06.title: Reflect a point
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-06.body:
The point $(8,0)$ is on $y=0.5x-4$, at distance $\sqrt{12^2+6^2}=\sqrt{180}$ from $M(-4,-6)$. Its image is on $y=2x+2$ at the same distance from $M$: $(x+4)^2+(2x+8)^2=180$ gives $(x+4)^2=36$, so $x=2$ or $x=-10$. The image $(2,6)$ gives a mirror through $M$ and the midpoint $(5,3)$: $y=x-2$. (The image $(-10,-18)$ would give a mirror of negative slope.) So $(a,b)=(1,2)$.

**Answer: $(1, 2)$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-07.title: Count factors of 5
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-07.body:
$20^{16}\cdot16^{20}=2^{32}\cdot5^{16}\cdot2^{80}=10^{16}\cdot2^{96}$. A power of $2$ never ends in $0$, so there are exactly $16$ trailing zeros.

**Answer: 16**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-08.title: Count digits by length
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-08.body:
Pages $1$–$9$ use $9$ digits and pages $10$–$99$ use $180$, leaving $2016-189=1827$ digits for three-digit pages: $\frac{1827}{3}=609$ pages, from $100$ to $708$.

**Answer: 708**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-09.title: Set up ages
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-09.body:
Let the son be $S$ and the father $3S$. Then $3S-6=5(S-6)$, so $S=12$ and the father is $36$. In $N$ years, $36+N=2(12+N)$ gives $N=12$, when the father is $48$.

**Answer: 48**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-09.title: Constant age difference
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-09.body:
The age difference never changes: it is $2S=24$. When the father is twice the son's age, the son's age equals the difference, $24$, so the father is $48$.

**Answer: 48**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-10.title: Shift by 15
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-10.body:
Write $N=15+k$. Then $N^2+N-4=k^2+31k+(15^2+15-4)=k^2+31k+236$, and $236=4\cdot59$, so we need $59\mid k(k+31)$. Since $59$ is prime, $k\equiv0$ or $k\equiv-31\equiv28\pmod{59}$. The least positive $k$ is $28$, so $N=43$. (Check: $43^2+43-4=1888=32\cdot59$.)

**Answer: 43**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-10.title: Sum of roots mod 59
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-10.body:
Mod $59$, the roots of $x^2+x-4$ sum to $-1$. One root is $15$, so the other is $-16\equiv43$. The values of $N$ that work are those $\equiv15$ or $43\pmod{59}$, and the least above $15$ is $43$.

**Answer: 43**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-11.title: Parametrize
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-11.body:
Since $2x$ and $2016$ are even, $5y$ is even, so $y=2t$ and $x=1008-5t$. We need $t\ge1$ and $1008-5t\ge1$, i.e. $1\le t\le201$. So $P=201$ (from $(1003,2)$ to $(3,402)$).

**Answer: 201**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-12.title: Inclusion–exclusion
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-12.body:
All assignments: $3^8=6561$. Those leaving a given club empty: $2^8$, for $3$ clubs: $3\cdot256=768$. Assignments leaving two clubs empty ($3$ of them) were subtracted twice, so add them back: $6561-768+3=5796$.

**Answer: 5796**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-13.title: Compare term by term
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-13.body:
Both sums have $1008$ terms, and each even term is $1$ more than the corresponding odd term. So the even sum is $1016064+1008=1017072$.

**Answer: 1017072**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-14.title: Complement
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-14.body:
Of the $900$ three-digit integers, $9$ have all digits equal and $9\cdot9\cdot8=648$ have all digits different. So $T=900-9-648=243$.

**Answer: 243**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-14.title: Patterns
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-14.body:
The integers have the form $XXY$, $XYX$ or $XYY$ with $X\ne Y$, where the leading digit is nonzero. For $XXY$ and $XYX$: $9$ choices of $X$ (nonzero) and $9$ of $Y$. For $XYY$: $9$ choices of the nonzero leading $X$ and $9$ of $Y\ne X$. Total $3\cdot81=243$.

**Answer: 243**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-15.title: Combine the inequalities
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-15.body:
Write them as $3x-y\ge0$ and $8x+4y\le40$ (multiplying the second by $4$). Subtracting the first from the second: $5x+5y\le40$, so $x+y\le8$, with equality only when both inequalities are equalities: $y=3x$ and $y+2x=10$, i.e. $(2,6)$.

**Answer: $(2, 6)$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-15.title: Corner of the region
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-15.body:
The region is bounded above by two lines meeting at their intersection $(2,6)$. Along $y=3x$ (for $x\le2$), $x+y=4x\le8$; along $y=10-2x$ (for $x\ge2$), $x+y=10-x\le8$. Every point of the region lies on or below one of these boundary lines at the same $x$, so $x+y\le8$, with the maximum only at $(2,6)$.

**Answer: $(2, 6)$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-17.title: Notice A + B
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-17.body:
With $A=2x-3$ and $B=3x+4$, $A+B=5x+1$. The equation $A^2+B^2=(A+B)^2$ reduces to $2AB=0$, so $2x-3=0$ or $3x+4=0$: $x=\frac32$ or $x=-\frac43$.

**Answer: $x=\frac32$ or $-\frac43$**

nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-18.title: Reflect M across the bisector
nyciml-2015-16-spring-sophfrosh-18.body:
Extend $MU$ to meet $\overline{GR}$ at $T$. Triangles $GUM$ and $GUT$ are congruent (ASA: common side $GU$, equal angles at $G$ since $GS$ bisects $\angle RGM$, right angles at $U$), so $GT=GM=11$ and $U$ is the midpoint of $MT$. Then $TR=17-11=6$. The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so $P$ is the midpoint of $MR$. In triangle $MTR$, $UP$ joins the midpoints of $MT$ and $MR$, so $UP=\frac12TR=3$.

**Answer: 3**
